title: MCP tools/list returns the full 46-tool set to unauthenticated callers, ignoring declared trust_tier
Bounty hunter attribution is spoofable: wallet_address binds the profile but is public and unauthenticated
llms.txt tells agents to clone 10 named trading agents; none of the 10 symbols exist on the platform
26 endpoints documented in llms.txt and agent-skills.json return 404
7 of the 11 MCP tool names documented in llms.txt do not exist, and the tool count differs across three sources
agent-card.json and agent-skills.json advertise different skill sets, and neither is a subset of the other
Published headline figures disagree across sources: commits, CLOB pairs, settlement chains and agent count
Bounty tracker reports 100% closure with no validation recorded: all 15 items read fixed, validated_at null on every one
The tool-catalog tier bug from report #46 is still live one tier up: TRUSTED is served 5 allied tools
llms.txt gives two different agent counts in its own text: 10 in one sentence, 11 in another
The stated agent-card/agent-skills subset model does not hold: 2 skill ids appear only in agent-skills.json

reason: Our check compared 'settlement on 10 chains' against the 16 chains /api/v1/swap/chains supports for swaps. Two different mechanisms; netting them is the collapsed-layer defect we report in others.

Measured our own probe method, not their contract. The original 18 were llms.txt rendering MCP tools as GET-able /mcp/v1/tools/<name> URLs, and those are gone. The 10 that remain are POST-only endpoints we probed with GET, where 405 is the correct answer.

Our check asserted the anonymous tool count equals the manifest total. That held only while tier gating was broken; once it was fixed, anonymous correctly returns 25 of 46 and our check reported their fix as a failure. Replaced by tests/mcp/test_trust_ladder.py.
Never a defect. The check is INCONCLUSIVE, not failing: llms.txt no longer links any tool names, so there is nothing to verify. It entered the ledger from a run before the claim was rewritten.
